claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Amy made an out-of-court statement to Karl.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(1) - Hearsay requires an assertion made out of court.

arguments.text: The statement asserts that the store needed to refund her and that marketing was deceiving.
arguments.evidence_span: that the store needed to refund her because their marketing had been decieving

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove Amy's belief that Karl was an employee, not to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) - Hearsay only applies when offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Amy believed that Karl was an employee of the store

arguments.text: When a statement is offered to show the declarant's state of mind or effect on the listener, it falls outside the definition of hearsay under FRE 801(c).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) and FRE 803(3) - Statements of state of mind or effect on listener are non-hearsay or admissible under an exception, but here it negates the definition.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Amy believed that Karl was an employee of the store
